neet_che_u14_t03_1.working: In but-2-ene each double-bond carbon carries two different groups (H and CH3), so cis and trans forms exist. Options 2, 3 and 4 each have one double-bond carbon bearing two identical groups, so none of them can show cis-trans isomerism.

neet_che_u14_t03_2.working: C4H10O has 4 alcohols: butan-1-ol, butan-2-ol, 2-methylpropan-1-ol and 2-methylpropan-2-ol. It has 3 ethers: methyl propyl ether, methyl isopropyl ether and diethyl ether. Total = 7.

neet_che_u14_t03_3.working: C2 and C3 are both chiral and their substituents differ, so the molecule is unsymmetrical. With no meso form, the number of stereoisomers is 2^2 = 4.

neet_che_u14_t03_4.working: A: butane and 2-methylpropane differ in carbon chain, so chain isomerism (III). B: the Cl changes position, so position isomerism (II). C: aldehyde versus ketone, so functional isomerism (IV). D: different alkyl groups on either side of the ether O, so metamerism (I).

neet_che_u14_t03_5.working: A is false: one carbon of CH2=CHCl carries two H atoms, so no geometrical isomerism. B is true: the cis isomer generally has the higher dipole moment. C is true: a racemic mixture is optically inactive. D is true: C5H12 has n-pentane, isopentane and neopentane. E is false: enantiomers rotate plane-polarised light in opposite directions. So B, C and D are correct.
